segments.text: Let's move on to the second posture called aramandi. In aramandi, the dancer places the heels close to each other with a little bit of space and turns out the toes in the opposite direction.
The toes have to be in the same line from one end to the other. And then the dancer squats halfway down to make sure the knees are in alignment with the toes.
And the dancer gets a diamond shape with her legs. This diamond shape must be maintained to have a good aramandi posture throughout the step.
Now that we have learned two basic postures, let's use these as the building blocks to learn our new adavus. This adavu series is called thattadavu — thatta means to strike and adavu means step.
The dancer takes the first two postures, starting with samapadam, and then sits down in aramandi, and strikes each foot once starting off with the right leg.
